## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Anumānapañha* ("Problems of Inference") constitutes section Mil 6.4.1 of the *Milindapañha*. As characterized by Oskar von Hinüber, it is a freestanding, unsubdivided section situated between parts of the work, wherein King Milinda and the elder Nāgasena meet again to discuss the Buddha as a single focal topic [von Hinüber 1996]. The dialogue exhibits stylistic differences from surrounding sections: Milinda addresses the monk with *bhante Nāgasena*, regularly concurs with Nāgasena's explanations, and canonical texts are quoted to support the reasoning [von Hinüber 1996]. Scholars have noted that the conceptual significance of *anumāna* ("inference") here reflects a distinct evolution in philosophical meaning compared to its earlier canonical usage in texts such as the Majjhima Nikāya's *Anumānasutta* [Watanabe 1983].
